pr_title: [Mono] Fix all the issues related to enabling WasmStripILAfterAOT
pr_body:
This PR enables IL trim by default for WASM apps, by solving the following major problems:

- There are various opcode which was translated into a function call. I modified the `call` goto logic to check if there is an AOT'ed version of the callee method. If there is, invoke that. If there isn't, interp compile the callee method.
- Move the logic of checking if a method is supported a JIT/AOT call from interpreter callback to `mini-runtime.c`. Because the callback was initialized with the desired logic only when `mono_use_interpreter` is set to true. See the following code 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8d4f8b86a742caba0f7640c013a2c1cefe10b146/src/mono/mono/mini/mini-runtime.c#L4629-L4632
However, in `driver.c`, `mono_use_interpreter` was not set to true during AOT compile time, even though `interp` was passed in as an AOT option. It would be set to true during AOT runtime. Alter this behavior is probably not desirable. Thus, I choose to move the checking logic to `mini-runtime.c`
- Set the trimmed assemblies with the same timestamp as the original assemblies. So that it won't trigger unwanted rebuild or re-AOT
- Added implementation of `g_fopen` to properly handle unicode string on windows. 
- Interpreter can't do JIT call for methods which require synchronization. Remove those methods from trimmable method list.
- Disabled tailcall optimization when calling trimmed methods.
- Do jitcall when encountering virtual tailcalls.
- Change of ILStrip task:
  - The trimmed assemblies were saved in a new folder with the same name as the original assembly.
  - Created an output variable `UpdatedAssemblies` with the updated path of assemblies. The trimmed assemblies are updated with their new path.
  - Updated the WASM build toolchain to replace the content of `_WasmAssembliesInternal` with `UpdatedAssemblies`
- Added the input parameter `WasmRuntimeConfigFilePath` for `WasmAppBuilderBaseTask`. Got rid of the logic to calculate the path of `runtimeconfig.json` file. Use the value of `WasmRuntimeConfigFilePath` instead. (Fixes #93692)
- Found two issues related to wasm build process. @radical fixed them.
  - #93680
  - Fixes #93689
- Blazor app is able to packages the trimmed assemblies, when `WasmStripILAfterAOT` is enabled.
- Added tests for wasm template app and blazor template app 

**Library size change for top 3 largest libraries:**
- System.Private.CoreLib.dll.br: 452k -> 316K
- System.Text.Json.dll.br: 109k -> 81k
- Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.dll.br: 69k -> 54k

issue_context.title: [wasm] dotnet.native.wasm was re-generated because the list of .o files in emcc-link.rsp is non-deterministic
issue_context.body:
dotnet.native.wasm was re-generated during incremental build, when it shouldn't. It was triggered because the list of .o files in emcc-link.rsp is non-deterministic.

Please re-enable corresponding tests upon fixing this.
comments:
Tagging subscribers to 'arch-wasm': @lewing See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
dotnet.native.wasm was re-generated during incremental build, when it shouldn't. It was triggered because the list of .o files in emcc-link.rsp is non-deterministic.
Author: fanyang-mono
Assignees: radical
Labels: `arch-wasm`
Milestone: 9.0.0
The issue was that `ILStrip`'s output assemblies were not in a deterministic order. They should be returned in the same order as the input. I have pushed fixes to the original PR - #90436 .

review_comments: Please log whether the file is being trimmed or being skipped, and why. See https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/25961d1156b3ed8cf684aaa9c56d78a8b2cecdfe/src/tasks/WasmAppBuilder/EmccCompile.cs#L251-L296 for an example.
Added.
Still don't think this is the right way, in a build system, build outputs like these should have later timestamps than the build inputs.
Without this, AOT generated bitcode files would have older timestamp than the assembly files. Then rebuild will trigger re-AOT, cause it thinks those assembly files have changed.
That seems to be a problem with other parts of the build which overwrites build files, its not possible to have correct build dependencies when files are overwritten.
TBH, I am not sure why other build files were overwritten but not triggering rebuild. This did fix the test failures tho. Do you have suggestions on fixing it in some other way?
Instead of overwriting the original files the item `_WasmAssembliesInternal` can be modified to have the updated paths.
How would that makes a difference? Those files will still be newer than the aot compiled byte code file. To my understanding, that's what triggered the rebuild.

I'm suggesting to not replace the original assembly files, and instead just change the paths to new ones in `_WasmAssembliesInternal`. That way rest of the build will be using the newly-trimmed assemblies, instead of the original ones.
The rest of the build are using the newly-trimmed assemblies, Because, the original ones got replaced with the trimmed ones right after IL strip task.
but if we don't replace the original ones then on a rebuild it should not trigger a rebuild. And this should ensure that we have the correct build dependencies, like Zoltan was talking about.
Oh I see what you mean. My worry for this is how we could guarantee tasks run after ILStrip step would always refer to the new ones?
`_WasmAssembliesInternal` is used by all the targets, that's the convention used in `WasmApp.Native.targets`, so that would ensure that the new ones are used.
We should fix this before merging.
